B is slightly less bad because it keeps the headline's wording and brand lettering.

Both lose the original's key element, the black-and-white praying-hands photo. Only white cloud outlines and plus marks are left, as near-invisible ghosts on white in the left half, so half the banner is dead space and the design is no longer recognisable; the quote text is readable and centred on the right but crowded toward the top edge. B is slightly worse because it adds a stray clipped grey bar along the top edge above the headline (a leftover sliver of the photo), while A at least keeps the plus marks faintly visible.

Both have the same broken layout. The robot vacuum is cropped so far that the product can't be recognised. The purple circle has shrunk to a small, orphaned quarter-shape that floats above the headline. 'Smart Home' is split from 'GADGETS' and pushed to the far right, so the headline reads out of order, and the thin frame line is cut off at the left. B is marginally better because its 'Smart Home' sits slightly further from the right edge, while A's crowds the canvas edge.

Both have the same broken symptom list: items run together ('Shortness of breath Dry / cough', 'Sore throat Headache'), so 6 symptoms read as 4 garbled lines and 'cough' is orphaned. Both also shrink the full-width yellow hashtag bar into a small badge and crop the doctor illustration on both sides. B's badge sits on the same left edge as the headline and list, so it aligns slightly better; A's centred badge floats off that left axis.

In A, 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' and the opening date are shrunk to unreadable specks. The pink dots float far above the headline, the white frame and card are left as an empty hollow box below the cropped stripe image, and there is a large dead gap above THE MINIMALIST. Its one saving point is that the reading order still runs presents → name → subtitle. B has the same unreadable presenter and date text and the same empty frame, but its reading order is worse: the presenter line falls below the headline in a void, the dots sit detached above DEAN COOPER, and THE MINIMALIST is pushed to the very bottom, cut off from the name it belongs to.

A breaks the design apart. The two food photos are shrunk to small thumbnails in a row next to empty frame outlines, a peach swatch and the plate sketch. The pasta pattern sits alone as a block in the middle, 'RESTAURANT' floats next to it, cut off from 'Cascadia', and the swash divider is blown up oversized. Still, the hero food photos are at least visible. B is worse: the background pasta pattern becomes the hero and fills most of the canvas. The food photos, frames and plate sketch are crushed into tiny specks in the footer, so the key imagery is lost entirely, and 'RESTAURANT' is stranded at the top left, far from 'Cascadia'.

A breaks the CTA apart: 'Join', 'WADE' and 'team' sit hundreds of pixels apart down the right edge. 'WE CREATE' is pushed beside 'MARKETING FUTURE' instead of above it, and the four decorative marks are lined up into a row that reads like an 'OIIX' logo. The maroon panel has become an empty box away from all the text. B also has the fake 'OIIX' row and the empty maroon box, but its headline stacks in the right order (though 'FUTURE' is slightly off the left axis). Its 'Join WADE team' stays on one line at the bottom, though the words are spread too far apart and sit on the busy photo.

Both use the same broken layout. The 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow sits at the top while the 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' headline is pushed to the very bottom, far below the owls, so the eyebrow and headline no longer read as one unit. The confetti is shrunk into a tiny band and large empty gaps are left above and below the owls. B is nearly identical, but its larger headline runs almost to the right edge ('BIRTHDAY'), so A's slightly better margins give it a marginal edge.

Both crush the decorative triangles and the wind-turbine icon into a cramped cluster at the left. The icon is shrunk to an illegible speck, the shapes are cropped into meaningless fragments, the red triangle sits almost against the headline, and the stray diagonal lines leave the right side mostly empty and unbalanced. B is marginally better because its headline is larger, its icon is slightly more readable and the triangle has a little more clearance from the text. A's red triangle almost touches the 'E' of ENERGY.

Both shrink the turbine hero to an illegible glyph jammed into the decorative triangles at the far right, overlapping them. They also leave a big empty gap between the left-hand headline and that cluster, and the original's line art is lost. A's headline is small and the turbine is barely visible. B's headline and turbine are slightly larger and easier to read, but the headline sits cramped against the top edge.

Both break up the SALE lantern stack in the same way. The S and A float apart from it, the L shrinks to a tiny glyph jammed against the E, and the white circles are left empty. The lanterns and clouds are crushed into unreadable clumps, so the brand motif is lost and the word doesn't read. B has a slightly larger headline but pushes the L/E collision tighter against the right canvas edge, so A is marginally less bad.

A: the SALE letters have come loose from their white medallion circles. The circles stack empty on the left, while S sits beside the headline and A, L and E are scattered across the bottom, so the hero word falls apart. The lanterns and clouds are crammed into the top right, leaving the left side empty. B is worse: its letters are scattered too and read S-A-E-L out of order. The tiny circle stack is empty, and all the decoration is shrunk into a thin central strip of illegible clutter, so the original symmetric framing is gone.

Both share the same broken layout. The cross is blown up into a huge, blurry raster that competes with the headline. The dates line is tiny and jammed against the headline's right edge. 'Worship & Bible Study' floats beside the cross with no shared alignment. The middle text column is cramped while the headline and illustration crowd their sides. A's cross is slightly larger and its illustration runs almost to the right edge. B leaves a little more right margin and has a marginally smaller cross, so it is only barely better.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical, with the same flaws. The background photo is cropped to the wrong side, so the product boxes become unreadable fragments at the right edge. The rules sit at the extreme top and bottom, so they no longer frame the text. 'food & drinks' is set as large as the headline and floats far below 'Order online', leaving a big empty gap. The headline is no longer dominant and the text lockup has fallen apart.

A: the 'food & drinks' subtitle is set larger than the 'Order online' headline, which flips the hierarchy. Both lines sit on top of the cup and box photo, and the short divider rules are stranded at the far left instead of framing the text. B is worse: 'Order online' and 'food & drinks' are split into two competing columns, so the reading order is lost. The oversized subtitle runs straight across the busy box image, and the single top rule floats with no relation to either text block.

Both break the original's composition the same way. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' kicker is cut off from its headline and stranded far left, the upside-down owl is shrunk into a tiny sticker in the middle of the canvas, and the blue owl is a speck at the far right, so the banner reads as scattered fragments and the headline is small. B is a little worse: the kicker is jammed against the left edge (about 5px), and a red confetti streamer cuts through 'KIDS' in the headline, while A keeps a reasonable left margin and its headline is cleaner.

Both are the same weak left-to-right strip. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' kicker is stranded far from the headline it belongs with, the owl's hat is cropped at the top edge, the right owl is shrunk to a tiny cramped icon, and confetti is scattered between the elements. A gives the kicker a better left margin, but red confetti streamers cut through 'KIDS DIRTHDAY'. B's headline is cleaner, but its kicker is jammed against the left canvas edge. B is marginally less bad because its headline has no collision.

Both break the brand lockup: 'HOHOHO' is at the top and 'AGENCY' at the bottom, with a band of cropped decorative fragments between them (half-cut red/cyan triangles, a clipped black circle and stray tree shapes). In both, 'Office Secret Santa' is small, wraps onto two lines and is jammed against the confetti, so the hierarchy and the original's centred composition are lost. B is marginally worse: its cyan ring and wavy lines are pushed left into the red triangle, and the small tree shapes and the enlarged bottom triangle crowd the subtitle and the gold dot more than in A.

Both lose the hero photo of the clasped hands, which is the core of the design. The quote shrinks to a tiny centered block on a mostly empty white strip, and the 'MAHATMA GANDHI' credit is too small to read and jammed under the last line. A leaves only stray cloud and scribble fragments at its edges. B adds a meaningless black rectangle above the headline, a leftover sliver of the photo, which makes it slightly worse.

A: the photo is cropped to a small square, and a white cloud blob and a large white cross cover the praying hands. Ghosted outline crosses and cloud fragments float on bare white, and the 'MAHATMA GANDHI' credit is shrunk to near-illegible type and pushed off to the far right edge, away from the quote. B: a white text panel covers almost the whole photo, so the hands (the key image) are lost and all that's left is a thin black strip. Cloud and cross fragments are scattered on the left, the cloud overlaps the strip, and there's a big dead gap between the quote and the credit. B's type hierarchy is cleaner, but A at least keeps some of the original imagery.

Both have the same layout and the same faults. The symptom list is garbled: 'Shortness of breath Dry / cough' wraps mid-item and 'Sore throat Headache' merges two symptoms on one line, so you can't count the six. The doctor illustration is cropped flat at the bottom. The CTA is small yellow text squeezed against the bottom edge, and the sparkle floats on its own. A is slightly more coherent because its hashtag badge is left-aligned on the same edge as the headline and list. B centres a small hashtag pill over left-aligned text, which keeps the original's centred bar but breaks the grid.

A: 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' is shrunk to an unreadable speck stranded mid-canvas above the image, and the date line is microscopic and left-jammed. The pink dots float far from the name, 'THE MINIMALIST' is pushed to the bottom away from the headline, and the cropped pattern leaves a hollow white frame box of dead space, so the reading order is jumbled. B has the same broken pieces: the presenter line is unreadable between the dots, the date is microscopic at the bottom-left, the white frame outline has lost its card, and there are big empty white gaps. However, its order (presenter, name, image, subtitle pill, date) follows the original sequence, and the subtitle pill is sized sensibly, so it is the less broken of the two.

Both share the same layout and the same faults. 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' sits alone at the top, far from 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' at the bottom, so the kicker and headline no longer read as one unit. The confetti is shrunk into a tiny strip under the kicker instead of scattered across the canvas, and big empty bands sit above and below the owls. B has slightly larger owls and its headline sits a little higher, but its brown owl's ear runs into the right edge, so neither is clearly better.

Both look almost the same, and both are broken. The wind-turbine icon, which was the hero, is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail and squeezed into a jumbled strip at the left with the green, blue and red triangles. The right third is left empty apart from a few stray hairlines, so the banner is lopsided. A is slightly better because its headline is a bit larger and has more space from the red triangle. In B the text sits right against the triangle's edge.

Both separate the 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow from its headline and push it to the far left, so the hierarchy breaks into scattered pieces. Both also crop the orange owl hard at the top edge and squeeze the blue owl into the right corner, leaving empty space on the left. B is slightly worse: a red confetti streamer cuts through the headline between 'KIDS' and 'DIRTHDAY', where A's slightly smaller headline stays clear of it.

Both drop the praying-hands photo, the original's key image, and turn the design into a white strip with tiny centred quote text. In both, the 'MAHATMA GANDHI' attribution is crammed against 'BOLT OF THE EVENING' at an illegible size, and the cloud and cross fragments float off to the sides at random. A is worse because of a stray black rectangle clipped at the top edge above the headline, which reads as a broken leftover of the photo; B is cleaner but still nowhere near shippable.

Both are nearly the same weak leaderboard. The photo is shrunk to a small, dim thumbnail on the left, and the headline still wraps to three short lines instead of running as one line across the banner. The white heart, the original's main brand shape, is reduced to a faint outline, and the URL is tiny and barely readable. In A the URL floats above a ghost heart in the top-right with nothing aligned to it. In B the URL sits inline with a small heart icon, which looks slightly more deliberate.

The two layouts are nearly identical. Both shrink the doctor illustration to a tiny figure while the sparkle grows into an oversized focal point that competes with it. Both break the headline awkwardly as '6 / SYMPTOMS', and the symptom list runs items together ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache'). A's hashtag badge keeps the original's yellow fill with dark text. B's badge looks recoloured and has less contrast, which weakens the brand slightly, so A wins by a small margin.

Both have the same structural problems. The #FLATTENTHECURVE bar has shrunk to a thin strip with tiny text that is hard to read. The symptom list has re-wrapped into run-on lines ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache'), so it no longer reads as six items. The list is also jammed against the top edge, the sparkle is blown up into a competing focal point, and the doctor's body is cut off flat at the bottom. B is slightly worse: its headline 'SYMPTOMS' is bigger and almost touches the doctor illustration, and its list sits even tighter to the top. A keeps a clear gap between the headline and the figure.

A keeps a sensible left-to-right order (presenter → DEAN COOPER → title pill), but the patterned background is reduced to a tiny thumbnail with an empty white card and dots inside, so the brand pattern is mostly lost. The 'OPENING JANUARY 1' line is very small and pressed against the thumbnail edge. B is broken: 'THE MINIMALIST' pill sits over the busy pattern strip, 'OPENING…' runs into the pill, 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' is tiny and comes after the name it introduces, there is a stray empty white frame, and the pink dots are stranded at the canvas edges.

Both break apart the original's signature layering, where the headline sat over the red T. The headline is now a tiny five-line stack wedged at the far left, the T floats alone on the right as a meaningless shape, and the middle of the banner is dead space. The tiny text and the loss of the stacked composition mean neither reads as the same design. A is slightly worse: its text sits jammed against the left edge and the T touches the top edge. B at least gives the text a small left margin and keeps the T off the top.

Both pull all text out of the label frame, leaving a large empty white cartouche, and shrink the lavender illustration into a tiny strip floating in a huge dead lower half. A is worse. It leaves orphaned divider rules stranded inside the empty frame, crams 'J'adore Paris / LAVANDER / SKINCARE' into one cramped row with tiny SKINCARE text, and sets HOMEMADE LOTION small and off-axis. B at least keeps the dividers with their text and gives LAVANDER and HOMEMADE LOTION more presence. Still, the brand lockup is jammed against the top edge and the frame is a meaningless blank box.

A: all the text has been pulled out of the label frame into a scattered left column ('LAVANDER' is weak, 'SKINCARE' is tiny, 'HOMEMADE LOTION' is shoved into the bottom-left corner). That leaves the frame as a large empty box with orphaned divider rules. The illustration row does survive at a readable scale along the bottom. B: the frame is empty and its divider rules spill past its right edge; one stray rule cuts through the shrunken illustrations. The text is strung across the top in a single row with no hierarchy, and the product art is reduced to an illegible thumbnail strip, so the original design is lost.

A keeps the copy in one cluster, but the alignments clash: the headline and teal line are left-aligned while the body copy is centered and shifted right. One divider floats to the right of the teal line and the other sits beside the contact text, the contact text is too small to read, and the top third is dead space. B scatters everything: the headline is jammed against the left edge, the body copy sits alone on the right, a divider floats at mid-left, the teal line breaks into two lines beside broken dash pieces, and the contact text is unreadably small at the far right edge, so there is no reading order or grouping.

Both break the design apart. The decorative frames, peach panel and pasta pattern are scattered as empty boxes and a floating tile. Both pasta photos shrink to thumbnail size. The orange divider strokes and the plate sketch are strung across the top like debris. A puts the 'Cascadia' / RESTAURANT / URL lockup on a clean baseline beside a big headline. B ties the orange divider to the headline, but it floats 'RESTAURANT' above and to the right of 'Cascadia' (wrong reading order, misaligned), and its photos are even smaller, so A is marginally less bad.

A: the white headline sits on a pale grey background with almost no contrast, so it is nearly unreadable. The red quote panel has shrunk to a meaningless small box, the skyline is a tiny strip, and the white author line on grey is barely visible. B has the same unreadable white-on-grey headline, and its top line collides with the decorative rules. B also leaves a large empty grey box as dead space, and the attribution is clipped at the top edge of the red panel. B keeps the red-panel-and-skyline motif better, but its clipped name and collisions make it slightly worse.

Both use the same weak banner layout. The 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is split off to the far left, away from its headline, which breaks the grouping. A loose confetti cluster fills the middle like dead space. The two owls are shrunk to small icons and jammed against the 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' headline, and the brown owl's ear nearly touches the 'K'. B is slightly worse: its larger eyebrow and owls push the eyebrow against the left edge and the headline against the right edge, and the owl meets the 'K', while A keeps a little more margin.

Both shrink the wind-turbine icon, which is the original's focal hero, to a tiny glyph. They also crush the green, red and blue triangles into a cramped strip along the top edge. The text block then fills the bottom with stray diagonal lines around it, so the icon-over-title hierarchy and the airy composition are lost. B centres the title the way the original does, while A's left-aligned text sits off-axis under a centred icon, so B is slightly less wrong.

Both are essentially the same broken layout. The 'MERRY' headline has shrunk to a tiny afterthought jammed among the icons at top right. The characters are reduced to a cramped grid of small stickers along the right half, while the left half of the canvas is empty dead space. 'DISCOUNT' is pushed into the bottom-right corner, so the original centered headline lockup is lost and the reading order runs backwards. The only difference is that A's DISCOUNT is a touch larger and sits slightly lower, which isn't a meaningful gap.

Both break the core concept the same way: the quote is pulled out of the framed illustration and set as a 1–2 word-per-line column (orphaned 'JUST', 'WEAR'), while the frame is shrunk to a small thumbnail that now shows a stray 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION' placeholder. The attribution 'CAROLYN MURPHY' sits under the image instead of under the quote, splitting the group. B sets the quote slightly larger, so it fills the left column a bit better, but that does not fix the shared structural flaws, so the two are effectively equivalent.

Both fail the same way: the diamond photo mosaic becomes one small square photo next to an empty white lattice of diamond outlines. The date diamond overlaps the photo's bottom edge, the address and date text is tiny, and the body copy is very small. A breaks the headline cleanly as 'SAVE / YOUR CITY', but its divider rule floats on its own under the empty lattice and the URL is pressed against the right edge. B leaves 'CITY' alone on the second line of the headline, and its rule and vertical URL are tucked awkwardly between the left diamond and the photo, so A is slightly less bad.

A just shrinks the original. The stripe block floats with dead white bands above and below, the white card is cut short, and the product list falls off the card onto the blue/red stripe seam, where tiny dark text sits across two colours with weak contrast. B rearranges the layout and gives the $49.99 price clear dominance with a legible product list. But it breaks the copy apart: 'for all drinkware on' becomes illegible fine print at the very bottom, cut off from the price it qualifies. The URL shrinks to an unreadable vertical sliver in the top-right corner, and the stripes become disconnected floating bars of uneven length.

Both lose the original's full-height colour stripes and white card. The stripes become two small stubby bars plus a stray grey slab, and the vertical URL shrinks to illegible micro-text (top-centre in A, wedged between the bars in B). 'for all drinkware on' is disconnected from $49.99. B is worse: 'WINE GLASSES' wraps into 'WINE / GLASSES', which reads as two separate list items and breaks the product list. A keeps the five-item list intact.

A breaks the headline into three lines with 'KEEP' stranded on its own line, and shrinks the cat illustration into a small island whose hard, flat bottom edge floats about 55px above the canvas, so the original full-bleed feel is lost and the space is lopsided. B keeps the original two-line headline break and a larger cat group, but the artwork's flat bottom still floats about 25px off the edge with a dead strip on each side, and there is too much empty space above the headline and between the headline and the cats.

Both break the original's stacked lockup in the same way. 'food & drinks' is pulled out of the rules, set larger than the 'Order online' headline so it competes with it, and runs over the busy kraft box photo. The headline is left-shifted and no longer centred between its two rules, which now frame empty space. B is marginally worse: its headline sits further off the rule axis and its subtitle pushes further onto the box image.

A: the quote is shrunk to small text squeezed into a narrow white gap on the left, jammed against the edge and the beige shape, while the large pink 'Ar' graphic takes over as the focal point, so the hierarchy is lost. B: it keeps the original's right-side quote, which is larger and readable on clean white, but the white panel crudely slices the pink/red graphics into cut-off fragments and the quote has little breathing room near the top edge of the panel.

A blows the headline up to four oversized lines. 'FURNITURE DESIGN' runs almost into the info boxes, the blue 'MODERN/FURNITURE' sits on a busy photo with weak contrast, and the left half feels overstuffed while the original's balance is lost. B keeps a three-line headline at a sensible size and stays closer to the original, but the headline drops to mid-canvas with dead space above it, the text still sits on a busy interior photo, and the lines break unevenly ('FESTIVAL' is left alone on the last line).

A sets the headline, window and venue details on one shared left edge, so it reads as one deliberate column. But the headline is small next to the huge window, the details are tiny and sit cramped right under the window, and the right-aligned date line breaks the left edge that the address line sets. B scatters the three parts onto three different axes: the headline is jammed into the top-left corner, the window is centred and the details sit in the bottom-right. That leaves no shared edge and uneven margins, and the headline and details are also undersized, so it looks arbitrary rather than designed.

Both are near-identical shrunk copies of the original crammed into a tiny banner: the event details on the right are reduced to illegibly small, ragged right-aligned text pushed against the canvas edge, and the stained-glass window shrinks to a minor icon. A leaves slightly more breathing room around the window and the right block; in B the window crowds the headline and the date/address text sits even tighter against the right edge.

Both break the design the same way: the dark panel sits empty on the left, while the headline and its gold frame have drifted right onto the busy triangle pattern, which hides the first letters ('rd-Winning / chitecture' in A). Gold text on gold pattern is unreadable and the panel/text pairing is gone. B is fractionally less clipped ('ard-Winning / rchitecture'), so it is very marginally less bad, but both are unusable.

Both candidates are essentially the same broken layout. The 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN' kicker has dropped below and to the left of 'London', so the headline reads out of order. The arrow chevrons are blown up into a huge, overlapping row of six that becomes the main focal point. The translucent panel is gone, so dark text sits directly on a busy, blurry, over-upscaled city photo. B only nudges 'London' and the tagline a few pixels left, which doesn't fix the scattered grouping or the chevron collision.

A is jumbled. The tagline is squeezed into an illegible 4-line stack in the left corner on a busy skyline, and 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN' sits to the right of 'London', which reverses the headline order. The two chevron groups collide in the middle, and large gaps are left between the fragments. B reads in order ('London' then the tagline then the chevrons) and its text is more legible, but it drops 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN', and the tagline runs right up against 'London' and the chevrons. All of B's text also sits directly on the busy city photo, with weak contrast, and the light panel behind the text is gone.

A is basically the original shrunk to fit, with no rearranging. Still, it keeps the dot patterns, the blue image band and the ampersand/BEDDING lockup with clear gaps between them. Its flaws: 'Baby Toddler' is tiny and hard to read at 50px tall, and BEDDING sits close to the right edge. B has more problems: it squashes the blue image into a thin sliver on the left, which leaves a large, dead dark area. It drops the dot texture, and it jams BEDDING right up against 'Toddler', so the lockup reads as one cramped, colliding string, again with 'Baby Toddler' too small to read.

Both fail the same way. The 'CREATIVE AGENCY' tagline is cut loose from the 'CLAYTONI' headline and pushed to the bottom. The two illustration clusters are shrunk into small, hard-cropped strips floating mid-canvas, leaving large empty navy areas above and below them. So the layout reads as scattered fragments rather than a portrait recomposition, and the art no longer frames the wordmark. A's illustrations sit closer to the canvas edges with uneven side margins. B's margins are slightly more even and its tagline sits marginally closer to the headline, so B is very slightly less bad.

A shrinks the decorative teeth into a row of tiny icons along the left edge that reads as debris, and the one-line 'DENTAL SERVICES' runs almost into the big tooth and the woman, who is cramped against the right edge. B keeps the teeth larger and bleeding off the top-left like the original, centres the headline with room on both sides, and keeps the tooth-and-woman group on the right. In B the woman is still small and cut off at the right edge, and the left teeth cluster looks a little crowded.

The two are nearly pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The headline breaks badly, with '6' stranded on its own line beside SYMPTOMS. The symptom list reflows into run-on lines ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache'), so the six items can't be counted. The doctor, the key image, shrinks to a tiny figure and is outweighed by an oversized white sparkle. The full-width yellow hashtag bar becomes a small badge, and the bottom band is cramped while the right side sits empty. The only visible difference is the hashtag badge: A's has slightly more padding and B's is a touch tighter, which isn't enough to separate them.

A: all copy (J'adore Paris, LAVANDER, SKINCARE, HOMEMADE LOTION) is strung along a top row outside the label frame, which sits empty except for orphaned divider rules; the illustration row is shrunk to a tiny, unreadable strip floating on the right, and the brand lockup and imagery are lost. B is also broken: the text is scattered down a left column with big gaps, LAVANDER is undersized, SKINCARE is tiny, the label frame is empty with stray rules, and the illustrations are spread out and pixelated. Still, B keeps the illustration band at a recognisable size and the text in reading order, so it is less bad.

Both break the original's main idea, where the quote sits inside the illustrated frame. The quote is now a narrow left column with one or two words per line ('JUST', 'WEAR' alone on a line). On the right is a small thumbnail that shows stray 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION' placeholder text inside the frame. 'CAROLYN MURPHY' is cut off from its quote and sits under the picture as if it were a caption. The two candidates differ only by a few pixels in the size of the illustration and the position of the author line, so neither is better.

Both break apart the striped-panel concept. The stripes shrink to stubby bars, a grey bar floats with no purpose, and the product list is bigger and heavier than the $49.99 price, so the hierarchy is wrong. A also splits 'WINE GLASSES' into two lines, so the list reads as six items with 'WINE' left on its own, and it squeezes the URL into an unreadable vertical sliver between the stripes. B keeps the list intact, but its URL is a tiny, unreadable rotated scrap stuck in the top-right corner. B is a little less broken.
